A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and provide readable main text and Appendices A–E. All fourteen figures and fifteen tables can be matched despite relocation and layout changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original multilingual counterfactual evaluations, data-augmentation experiments, human translation assessments, and appendix robustness analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results, including the human assessments and appendix robustness and error-filtering experiments.

M1.justification: The three-step, one-shot counterfactual generation procedure, direct and translation-based variants, model choices, and augmentation procedures are unchanged. Appendix prompts are also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate XNLI and SIB200 across the same six languages. Appendix E.3 retains the same robustness scenarios using SNLI-derived and manually created SIB200 counterfactuals.

E2.justification: The evaluated generator set remains Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma3-27B, and Llama3.3-70B. Direct-versus-translated comparisons and the base-versus-augmented mBERT comparisons retain the same participants, including in the appendices.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the written TS metric specification: v2 divides the embedding dot product by the counterfactual norm twice, unlike v1's cosine similarity. This is a non-equivalent reported formula; implementation changes or reruns are not established. Other evaluation settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The cross-lingual edit analyses, four error categories, human-counterfactual robustness evaluations, and error-filtering experiment in Table 15 already appear in v1 and are retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Seed information, including seed 42 in Appendix E.3.2, is unchanged. Tables 9–10 retain the same correlation and inter-annotator agreement reporting with p-values; no additional repeated-run or uncertainty reporting appears.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged, including Table 1's generation scores and Tables 13–15's robustness, augmentation, and filtering results. Rearranged displays introduce no new result entries.

T1.justification: The expanded TS definition in Section 4.1 is mathematically non-equivalent to v1: cosine similarity requires the product of the original-input and counterfactual norms, whereas v2 repeats the counterfactual norm. Other mathematical definitions are unchanged.

C1.justification: The main contributions and conclusions are retained. V2 adds the prominence of copy-paste errors to the introduction, but this claim was already stated in v1's conclusion.

C2.justification: Interpretations of translation quality, cross-lingual editing, error mechanisms, and limited augmentation benefits remain unchanged, as do the substantive limitations. The English-prompt rationale moves from Appendix A to Section 3.1.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-and-evaluation-results access link on the first page and an explicit mGPT checkpoint link in Section 4.1. Existing prompts, preprocessing instructions, hyperparameters, and inference-time information are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds references on multilingual conversational XAI and iFlip, removes Nguyen et al. (2025), and changes the quantization/explainability references in Limitations. The overall research gap and positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: Changes include affiliation and acknowledgment edits, moving the English-prompt rationale into Section 3.1, incorporating a translation caveat from a footnote into the prose, and limited wording refinements. The overall section structure is retained.

P2.justification: Table 1's subtables and appendix Tables 13–14 change from stacked to side-by-side arrangements. Existing figures are resized or relocated, and appendix floats reflow; figure and table membership and substantive display content remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: New access links improve reproducibility documentation, and side-by-side tables facilitate comparison. However, v2 replaces v1's correct cosine-similarity definition with a non-equivalent expression, without clarifying whether the error is confined to typesetting. With unchanged empirical evidence, these benefits and the unresolved technical ambiguity leave the net quality direction uncertain.
